title: Continuous transfinite towers of categorical fibrations compute coherent limits
statement: Use the universes, simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent diagrams, cores and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and isofibrations of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Fix a small nonzero ordinal $\lambda$ and a strict inverse diagram $X:\lambda^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$ of small quasicategories. Assume that $X_{\alpha+1}\to X_\alpha$ is an isofibration whenever $\alpha+1<\lambda$, and that, for every nonzero limit ordinal $\beta<\lambda$, the canonical map $X_\beta\to\lim_{\alpha<\beta}X_\alpha$ is a simplicial isomorphism. Then the degreewise simplicial limit $L=\lim_{\alpha<\lambda}X_\alpha$ is a quasicategory and its projection cone is a limit cone in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. For every small simplicial set $K$, the canonical equality $\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)=\lim_{\alpha<\lambda}\operatorname{Fun}(K,X_\alpha)$ presents a limit in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ as well. These comparisons are induced by projections and are natural in maps of continuous inverse diagrams and restrictions of $K$. No surjectivity on objects is assumed.

source.place: Appendix A.2.9, especially Proposition A.2.9.19, Example A.2.9.22, and Corollaries A.2.9.24(ii) and A.2.9.25(2): well-founded inverse Reedy diagrams and injective fibrancy. The statement is the agent-formulated continuous-ordinal specialization in the Joyal model, extending the sequential case of Kerodon Example 7.6.5.10 (03HT), read online.
